text: {"question":"What is the difference in the Hubble constant value obtained from the corrected Pantheon+ sample when the upper Hubble‑diagram redshift limit is set to 0.151 versus when it is increased to 0.20, and how does this compare to the DES‑DOVEKIE offset measured at the same redshift limit?","reference_answer":"At zHD,max = 0.151 the corrected Pantheon+ gives H₀ ≈ 73.55 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, rising to ≈ 73.99 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ at zHD,max = 0.20, a ΔH₀ of about 0.44 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹. The DES‑DOVEKIE offset, fixed at 0.151, is ≈ 0.44 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, matching the increase in H₀ from the Pantheon+ sample when the redshift limit is raised."}
